method: I split the anchors' rate of any nuclear use killing over 1,000 people (0.7%/yr forecast, 1.8%/yr pessimistic, tail-nuclear-grid.json) into wars, per year forecast/pessimistic: Russia-NATO war with a large-scale attack on Europe 0.07/0.25% (the anchors' own rate); Russian limited use on NATO Europe 0.03/0.10%; Russian use in Ukraine 0.17/0.45%; US-China large-scale war 0.025/0.08% and limited US-China use 0.10/0.22% (ONN and Swift Centre, March 2026: 1.3% by 2030 for any US-China exchange, about 0.28%/yr, shaded toward superforecasters for the forecast); India-Pakistan war with about 100 warheads or more 0.03/0.10% and smaller exchanges 0.07/0.15%; North Korean use 0.10/0.25%; use on Israel 0.02/0.08%; China-India 0.005/0.015%; Russia-China 0.003/0.01%; non-state 0.06/0.10%. The parts sum to 0.68% and 1.8%. Dyad shares were checked against the PS21 expert survey (2015) and the Atlantic Council Global Foresight survey (Nov-Dec 2025). For each country, nuclearNear = sum over wars of rate x weight x share alive one hour after the first detonation, where the weight is the chance the country is struck in a way that collapses power, supply and care nationally (every household counts, as in the anchors) plus, for countries hit only lightly, the share of urban households inside a damaged area or plume. Survival is 0.88 (US anchor) or 0.82 (Western Europe anchor) for heavily targeted countries, higher where targets are few or only plumes arrive. With US weights 0.72 (Russia-NATO) and 0.75 (US-China) the US anchor is reproduced; the population-weighted mean of weight x survival over 18 Western European countries is 0.74 against the anchor's 0.85 x 0.82 = 0.70. nuclearFar = any use less the rate of wars that strike the country at all, as the anchors do. falloutScale is the mean fallout death risk per counted household relative to the US 10,000 micromorts, judged from targets (ground bursts on hard targets upwind of cities), housing (light frame vs masonry or concrete) and winds; the triple is the uncertainty of the ratio, not of the absolute risk.

countries.name: Australia

nuclearNear.forecast.basis: Struck only at Pine Gap, North West Cape, Darwin or HMAS Stirling, which Australian governments accept as targets (Tanter, https://nautilus.org/briefing-books/australian-defence-facilities/possibilities-and-effects-of-a-nuclear-missile-attack-on-pine-gap/): US-China war 0.025%/yr x 0.6 x 0.015 of urban households in the area, plus Russia-NATO 0.07% x 0.3 x 0.005, plus limited US-China use, x 0.9 alive, plus 1e-6.

nuclearNear.pessimistic.basis: Pessimistic war rates (0.08%, 0.25%, 0.22%) and twice the share of households, with Darwin and Perth fully in play.

nuclearFar.forecast.basis: 0.7%/yr any use (anchor) minus 0.04% of wars that strike Australian facilities.

nuclearNear.falloutScale.basis: Only households near the facilities count, so their mean exceeds the US all-household mean; a ground burst on Pine Gap with southerly winds would be lethal in Alice Springs (Tanter); brick houses shield better than US light frame.

countries.notes: Reached only through a US-China or global US-Russia war that strikes the joint facilities; no published forecast names Australia.

nuclearNear.falloutScale.basis: Counted households are under plumes 200-400 km downwind of German and Italian bases, so dose arrives late and decayed; masonry housing.

countries.notes: Neutral; exposed as downwind of a European war.

openQuestions: falloutScale triples express uncertainty in the ratio to the United States, not in the absolute dose. Multiplying them with the US 1,500-10,000-60,000 triple as independent quantities would double-count the shared uncertainty; scaling the US triple by the ratio's middle value is closer to what I mean.

For South Korea, Israel, the Philippines, Australia and Mexico, most nuclearNear probability is a smaller attack in which only households in a damaged area or plume count. The presets' windows and leave options describe national collapse after a large-scale attack, so they overstate durations and understate leaving for these countries.

nuclearFar follows the anchors in subtracting every war that strikes the country at all, including small strikes that miss the household; read literally, the definition would leave those in nuclearFar. The difference is at most 0.04 points.
Every NATO Europe figure moves one-for-one with the anchors' 0.07%/0.25% war rate; the country weights only spread it.
nuclearFar varies only from 0.0059 to 0.007 (forecast); the integrator could leave it at the preset values with no visible change.
